Esther: Courage for Such a Time

Reference: The Book of Esther

Big Idea: God places us exactly where He wants us, and He gives us courage to do what is right.

Teacher Quick Reference

⏱️
Lesson: Esther: Courage for Such a Time
Scripture: The Book of Esther
Big Idea: God places us exactly where He wants us, and He gives us courage to do what is right.
Three Main Points:
  1. Esther, a Jewish orphan, was chosen to be the Queen of Persia.
  2. An evil official named Haman plotted to destroy all the Jews.
  3. Mordecai warned Esther that she was made queen 'for such a time as this.'
  4. Esther bravely approached the king uninvited, risking her life.
  5. God used Esther's courage to save His people from destruction.
Activity: Royal Protocol (Active Listening Game)
Memory Verse: Esther 4:14
Take-Home Truth:
"God put me where I am for a reason, and He will help me be brave."

Teacher Preparation

Before class:

  • Read the Book of Esther. It is a thrilling, dramatic narrative.
  • Focus on the conversation between Mordecai and Esther in chapter 4.
  • Prepare the “Throne” and “Golden Scepter” for the Royal Protocol activity.
  • Write the memory verse on the board.
  • Decide which age adaptation will work best for your classroom.

[!IMPORTANT] A note for the teacher The book of Esther deals with the heavy theme of genocide (Haman’s plot to destroy the Jews). While we don’t need to dwell on the gruesome details with children, we must not soften the reality of the danger Esther faced. Her statement, “If I perish, I perish,” is one of the greatest declarations of faith in the Bible. Emphasize that God’s invisible hand was protecting His people the entire time.

Opening Activity: The Right Place at the Right Time

Ask the children: “Have you ever been in the exact right place at the exact right time? Like catching a glass right before it falls off the table, or finding a lost dog just as its owner was looking for it?”

Allow a few answers.

Explain: “Sometimes people call that a ‘coincidence.’ But as Christians, we know that God is in control of everything. Today we are going to learn about a girl who ended up in a massive palace, wearing a royal crown, at the exact moment she needed to be there to save millions of people.”

The Bible Story

1. The Orphan Queen

Many years after Israel was conquered, a large number of Jewish people were living in the powerful empire of Persia. One of them was a young orphan named Esther, who was raised by her older cousin, Mordecai.

King Xerxes, the ruler of Persia, was looking for a new queen. He gathered all the most beautiful young women in the empire. Out of everyone, the king chose Esther! She was crowned Queen of Persia. But she kept a secret: she didn’t tell anyone she was Jewish.

2. Haman’s Evil Plot

The king had an official named Haman. Haman was very proud and demanded that everyone bow down to him. But Mordecai (Esther’s cousin) refused to bow to anyone except God.

Haman was so furious that he didn’t just want to punish Mordecai. He tricked the king into signing a law that on a specific day, all the Jewish people in the entire empire would be destroyed. The king signed the law with his special ring, meaning it could never be changed.

3. For Such a Time as This

When Mordecai heard the terrible news, he tore his clothes and cried bitterly. He sent a message to Queen Esther, begging her to go to the king and ask him to stop the law.

Esther was terrified. She sent a message back: “Everyone knows that if any person goes into the king’s inner court without being invited, there is only one law: they will be put to death. The only way to live is if the king extends the golden scepter.” (Esther 4:11). The king hadn’t called for her in thirty days!

Mordecai sent back one of the most famous messages in the Bible:

“For if you remain silent at this time, relief and deliverance for the Jews will arise from another place, but you and your father’s house will perish. And who knows but that you have come to your royal position for such a time as this?” (Esther 4:14, BSB)

Mordecai was saying, “Esther, God will save His people with or without you. But what if God made you the queen specifically so you could be the one to do it?”

4. If I Perish, I Perish

Esther had to make a choice. Stay safe and quiet, or risk her life to do the right thing? She asked all the Jews to fast and pray for her for three days. Then she said:

“I will go to the king, even though it is against the law. And if I perish, I perish.” (Esther 4:16, BSB)

Esther put on her royal robes and walked into the inner court. The king looked at her. Her heart must have been pounding. Slowly, the king smiled… and held out the golden scepter! Esther was safe.

5. The Great Rescue

Esther didn’t just blurt out her request. She wisely invited the king and Haman to two special banquets. At the second banquet, the king asked, “What is your petition, Queen Esther?”

Esther bravely revealed her secret. She told the king that she was Jewish, and that the evil Haman had planned to destroy her and all her people.

The king was furious! He ordered Haman to be taken away and punished. Because the original law couldn’t be canceled, the king wrote a new law allowing the Jewish people to defend themselves. God’s people were saved, all because one young woman had the courage to speak up.

The Deeper Meaning

The book of Esther never uses the word “God.” Why? Because the author wanted to show us that even when God is invisible, He is invincible. Even when we don’t hear God speaking from a burning bush or see Him parting the Red Sea, He is actively moving the pieces of history to protect His people.

God positioned Esther on the throne. God kept Mordecai safe. God made sure the king couldn’t sleep one night so he would read a book that proved Mordecai was a hero (Esther 6). God is the invisible Director of the play, and He is always working things together for good.

Three Things to Remember

1. God is Working Behind the Scenes

Just because you can’t see God doesn’t mean He isn’t working. He is always setting things up to protect His children. Teacher Question: How does it help you to know that God is in control even when things seem scary or out of control?

2. Bravery Means Trusting God

Esther was terrified. She literally thought she might die. But bravery isn’t the absence of fear; it’s doing the right thing while you are afraid. Teacher Question: What is the difference between not being scared and being brave?

3. You Are Here for a Reason

God didn’t just place Esther on a throne for a reason. He put YOU in your school, in your family, and in your neighborhood for a reason, too. Teacher Question: How can you help the people around you in the specific place God has put you?

Age Adaptations

Preschool (Ages 3-5)

Younger Children

For younger children (ages 5–7), focus on Esther’s bravery and God’s protection.

Simplified concepts:

  • Esther was a young girl who became a beautiful queen.
  • A mean man named Haman wanted to hurt Esther’s family and friends.
  • Esther had to go talk to the king to stop the mean man, but she wasn’t allowed to go unless the king called her.
  • She was very scared, but she prayed and was brave.
  • The king was happy to see her! She saved her people.

Developmentally appropriate questions:

  • What did the king hold out to show Esther she was safe? (A golden scepter).
  • What should we do when we are scared to do the right thing? (Pray and ask God to make us brave).
Upper Elementary (Grades 4-6)

Older Children

For older children (ages 8–11), focus on Mordecai’s challenge (“for such a time as this”) and the concept of God’s invisible providence.

Deeper discussion: Pre-teens are starting to wonder about their own purpose in life. Mordecai’s challenge to Esther is incredibly empowering for a young person wondering if their life matters.

Discussion Scenarios:

  • Scenario 1: You are sitting at a lunch table and all your friends start making fun of a kid who isn’t there. You know it’s wrong, but if you speak up, they might make fun of you next. How does Esther’s story help you in that moment?
  • Concept: Notice that Mordecai said, “If you remain silent… deliverance will arise from another place.” God’s plan to save His people wasn’t going to fail just because Esther was scared. But Esther would have missed out on the blessing of being used by God. God invites us to be part of His plan!

Discussion Questions

Understanding

  1. What was Esther’s big secret when she became queen?
  2. Why did Haman hate Mordecai so much?
  3. What rule did Esther break when she went to see the king?
  4. What did the king hold out to Esther to spare her life?
  5. What happened to Haman at the end of the story?

Thinking

  1. Why do you think the author of this book never used God’s name? What were they trying to teach us?
  2. What did Mordecai mean when he said, “for such a time as this”?
  3. Why did Esther ask everyone to fast (and pray) for three days before she went to the king?
  4. Did Esther do the right thing immediately, or did she have to be convinced?

Personal Application

  1. Has there ever been a time when you were scared to tell the truth or do the right thing?
  2. If God put you in your specific school or neighborhood “for such a time as this,” what do you think He wants you to do there?
  3. Who can you pray for this week who needs help or protection?

Activity Time

Activity Resource: Royal Protocol View Standalone →

Type: Active Listening Game
Time: 10 minutes
Group Size: Any
Materials:

  • A chair (the “Throne”)
  • A stick or rolled-up piece of paper (the “Golden Scepter”)

Purpose

To help children understand how terrifying it was for Esther to approach the king uninvited, by playing a game where breaking “royal protocol” has immediate consequences.

Setup

  1. Place the “Throne” at the front of the room.
  2. The teacher sits on the throne holding the “Golden Scepter” (hidden behind their back).
  3. Have all the children line up at the back of the room.

Exact Instructions

  1. Explain the rules: “In ancient Persia, the king had a very strict rule. If you walked into his throne room without being invited, the guards would take you away! The ONLY way you could live is if the king pointed his Golden Scepter at you.”
  2. Tell the children they must try to cross the room to the king.
  3. When the teacher says, “Approach!” the children can take steps forward.
  4. When the teacher says, “The King is looking!” the children must freeze instantly.
  5. If anyone moves while the king is looking, the teacher yells, “Guards!” and that child must run back to the starting line.
  6. The Scepter Twist: If a child gets all the way to the throne, the teacher will either bring out the Golden Scepter and point it at them (they win and stand next to the king), or keep it hidden (they are “banished” and must go back to the start).

Discussion

Ask: “Was it scary not knowing if the king was going to point the scepter at you?” “Imagine playing this game for real, where your actual life was on the line. Would you be brave enough to go see the king?”

Connection Back to the Bible Story

Explain: “Esther wasn’t playing a game. She knew that walking into King Xerxes’ throne room could mean death if he didn’t hold out the golden scepter. But she chose to be brave because she knew it was the only way to save her people.”

Craft Time

Activity Resource: Queen Esther's Crown View Standalone →

Materials:

  • Yellow or gold construction paper (cut into long strips)
  • Stickers, sequins, or stick-on gems
  • Markers or crayons
  • Stapler or tape (for the teacher to fit the crowns)

Purpose

To give children a tangible reminder of Esther’s royal position, and how God placed her in the palace “for such a time as this.”

Setup

  1. Cut the yellow or gold construction paper into long strips (about 3 inches wide and the length of the paper). You will need two strips stapled together to fit around a child’s head.
  2. Cut a zig-zag pattern into the top of the strips to look like a crown.

Instructions

  1. Decorate: Give each child a flat crown strip. Have them decorate it to look as royal as possible using markers, stickers, or stick-on gems.
  2. The Verse: Have older children write (or help younger children write) “For Such a Time as This” on the front of their crown.
  3. Assemble: When they are finished decorating, the teacher should wrap the crown around the child’s head to measure it, and then staple or tape the ends together so they can wear it!
  4. Wear it: Have the children put on their crowns and sit like brave kings and queens.

Discussion While Crafting

  • “Did Esther become the queen by accident, or did God plan it?” (God planned it perfectly).
  • “Was it scary for Esther to talk to the King?” (Yes, it was against the law!).
  • “When you wear this crown, remember that God has placed you exactly where you are—in your school, in your family, and in your neighborhood—for a reason. You can be brave like Esther!”

Memory Verse

Esther 4:14 (BSB)
”…And who knows but that you have come to your royal position for such a time as this?”

Practical Way to Teach:

  • Create a “Crown” motion for “royal position” (hands on head like a crown).
  • Create a “Time” motion for “time as this” (tap wrist like a watch).
  • Repeat the verse, replacing the word “royal position” with where the kids are right now (e.g., “…you have come to the 3rd grade for such a time as this!” or “…you have come to this school for such a time as this!”).

Application

You might not be a king or a queen, but God has given you a “royal position” as His child. This week, when you see someone being left out or treated unfairly, don’t stay silent. Remember that God put you in that exact room, at that exact time, to show His love.

Take-Home Challenge

Take a piece of paper and write “For Such a Time as This” on it. Tape it to your bedroom door. Every time you walk out of your room this week, ask God to use you to help someone today.

Closing Thought

Esther showed us that true courage isn’t about not being afraid. True courage is saying, “God put me here, and even if it costs me everything, I will do what is right.” We serve a God who is always working behind the scenes. You never have to worry if your life matters, because the Creator of the universe has placed you exactly where He wants you.

Closing Prayer

“Heavenly Father, thank You for the story of Esther. Thank You that You are always working behind the scenes to take care of us. Lord, sometimes we are scared to do the right thing or to stand up for people who need help. Give us the courage of Esther. Help us to believe that You have put us exactly where we are for such a time as this. In Jesus’ name, Amen.”

ESTHER: COURAGE FOR SUCH A TIME
The Book of Esther

Big Idea

God places us exactly where He wants us, and He gives us courage to do what is right.

Memory Verse

”…And who knows but that you have come to your royal position for such a time as this?” — Esther 4:14 (BSB)

Three Points

  1. God is Working Behind the Scenes

Opening

The Right Place at the Right Time (Discussion about coincidences vs. God’s timing).

Activity

Royal Protocol (Active game about the risk of approaching the king).

Closing

Pray for the courage to stand up for what is right, trusting in God’s perfect placement of our lives.
